thread:
alice.m: sec-bot just flagged an unusual S3 access pattern. says cross-account read via a VPC endpoint. bucket=redwood-prod-artifacts, principal=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root, vpce=vpce-0abc123def :eyes:
sec-bot: detection: s3:ListBucket on redwood-prod-artifacts from arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root (sourceVpc=vpc-0aa11bb22) timestamp=2026-03-20T09:12:31Z ct_event_id=evt-0a1b2c3d4e
ben.j: copying alert here. do we have recent changes to that bucket policy or vpce policy?
charlie.s: not aware of intentional cross-account access. that bucket should be internal only. can someone paste the bucket policy and vpce policy?
dana.ops: pulling policy now. running: `aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-prod-artifacts` and `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoint --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0abc123def`
dana.ops: bucket policy has a statement allowing `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root` (looks like a leftover from an old partner onboarding).
ben.j: ok containment ASAP: 1) remove principal from bucket policy or add explicit Deny for NotPrincipal to block external accounts; 2) restrict VPC endpoint policy to our account only; 3) rotate any exposed credentials if found.
charlie.s: agree. I'll push the deny patch to the bucket policy now. quick deny snippet we can apply (patch via console or CLI):
```
{
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "DenyCrossAccountVpcEndpointAccess",
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:*",
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-artifacts","arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-artifacts/*"],
      "Condition": {
        "StringNotEquals": {"aws:PrincipalAccount":"12345678901234567890"}
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
charlie.s: (that's intentionally strict — will block non-account principals regardless of vpce).
dana.ops: I also set the VPC endpoint policy to deny any access for principals outside our org. running `aws ec2 modify-vpc-endpoint --vpc-endpoint-id vpce-0abc123def --policy-document file://vpce-policy.json`
sec-bot: audit: CloudTrail shows ReadObject/ListBucket events at 2026-03-20T09:11:58Z and 09:12:20Z from that principal. no PutObject detected. detected access used sse-kms with key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:999999999999:key/abcd-1234.
ben.j: KMS note: if objects were encrypted with customer-managed key, we need to check the key policy for that key as well. can someone run `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <key-id> --policy-name default`?
dana.ops: grabbing it. key policy currently allows the account root and a few roles. no external principals listed. good.
alice.m: containment done? any ongoing reads?
dana.ops: after deny applied, no further ListBucket events from that principal. CloudTrail shows last event at 09:12:20Z, then nothing.
charlie.s: good. next: scope of impact — any objects downloaded? sec-bot only shows ListBucket and GetObject attempts that returned 200 for a few small artifacts at 09:12:20Z. logging shows 3 GetObject responses 200.
ben.j: we should assume exfil possible. action items: 1) rotate any secrets that reference those artifacts (deploy keys, CI tokens); 2) rotate KMS key or rekey and re-encrypt if secrets stored; 3) create an incident ticket for legal/comms to review.
dana.ops: I've started an internal ticket INC-2026-342 in our tracker, pinging infra, platform, and compliance.
charlie.s: also add permanent monitoring: enable S3 data event logging to CloudTrail for that bucket (if not already), and add an alert rule for ListBucket from principals outside our org.
sec-bot: recommendation: create an allowlist on bucket policy using `aws:PrincipalOrgID` condition to lock to our org and use access points for internal-only access.
alice.m: good suggestion. ben, charlie — can you draft a short remediation runbook for the on-call? include commands we ran, rollback steps, and post-incident checks.
ben.j: on it. will include CLI commands we used and KMS rotation checklist.
charlie.s: I'll own postmortem and follow-up controls: 1) inventory buckets with cross-account principals; 2) run automated scan for vpce policies allowing external principals; 3) add PR checklist item to prevent adding external principals without review.
dana.ops: also proposing an automated guardrail: deny any new bucket policy that references principals outside our account via a Terraform policy check in CI.
alice.m: thanks team. immediate containment = done. leaving the thread open for the postmortem draft and legal/compliance input. :thumbsup:
